title: Supplier acceptance roadmap and SLA decisioning - BlueOak Financial kickoff
summary: Kickoff to align on vendor acceptance path: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing approval steps, and a pilot timeline. Security asked for SOC2 artifacts and KMS details; procurement asked for commercial path and approval owners. Action: Redwood to share redline suggestions, SOC2 report link, and pilot SLOs; BlueOak to confirm decision committee and target budget for Q4 pilot.
next_steps: Jordan to send MSA redline suggestions and commercial term sheet by 2026-10-21
Maya to share SOC 2 Type II attestation PDF and KMS integration note by 2026-10-20
BlueOak to confirm decision committee and budget by 2026-10-25
Schedule technical pilot kickoff (30 days) once MSA terms agreed
action_items: owner:Jordan Patel, item:Send proposed MSA redlines + commercial term sheet, due_date:2026-10-21
owner:Maya Chen, item:Provide SOC2 Type II report, KMS/HSM integration note, and typical architecture diagram, due_date:2026-10-20
owner:Nadia Grey, item:Review DPA exception list and flag three must-haves, due_date:2026-10-23
owner:Jamal Patel, item:Provide estimated pilot capacity (GPU hours) and sample request profile, due_date:2026-10-22
owner:Liam O'Connor, item:Confirm procurement approval owners+timeline, due_date:2026-10-25
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Alright thanks everyone for joining, we'll wait a minute for folks to dial in. Uh yeah, appreciate you carving out time.
[00:18] Liam (BlueOak): Hi all, Liam here from procurement, we have Sofia from security and Jamal in platform, Nadia from legal joining in a sec. Sound good.
[00:30] Jordan: Great, quick agenda: align on vendor acceptance path, MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets and pricing approval. Then call out next steps and owner.
[00:45] Maya (Redwood SE): Hi hi everyone, I'm Maya, I'll handle the technical questions around private vs dedicated and how our KMS flows work.
[00:57] Sofia (BlueOak): Hi, thanks. From security perspective primary asks are SOC2, encryption-at-rest, audit logs, and data residency. We also want to understand RBAC and SSO options.
[01:12] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll go into each. Ethan from our success team is on to talk pilot timeline and onboarding.
[01:24] Ethan (Redwood CSM): Hey all. Quick note: typical pilot is 4 weeks, we can compress if contract gating is quick.
[01:35] Nadia (BlueOak Legal): Joining now, sorry for the delay.
[01:38] Jordan: No worries. Ok first MSA/DPA: Liam, what's your procurement path look like? Decision committee?
[01:46] Liam: We have a three-step gating: procurement review, legal redlines, and then exec sign-off if there are pricing or term deviations. Budget is on the table now but we need clarity on SLA and indemnity.
[02:02] Jordan: Understood. On indemnity and liability we typically align to enterprise practice; we'll share our standard MSA and highlight where BlueOak may want exceptions. We can propose a cap tied to fees or mutual indemnities.
[02:18] Nadia: We will flag any carve-outs for regulated data — BlueOak is under PCI/financial regs. DPA needs strong controls; we may request data residency constraints.
[02:29] Maya: For data residency we support region pinning in Dedicated and some Private deployments; hosted has region controls but not hard-residency guarantees unless on a private VPC.
[02:42] Jamal: So if we need hard residency for sensitive workloads we should be looking at Redwood Dedicated or Private? What's the cost delta?
[02:51] Jordan: Correct. Dedicated gives predictable capacity and region isolation. Pricing delta depends on commit size; we'll include a ballpark in the term sheet.
[03:03] Liam: On SLA, our ops team needs 99.9% uptime for production flows and an SLO for tail latency, say 95th percentile under X ms. Can you meet that?
[03:14] Maya: We can commit to SLA tiers. 99.9 is typical for Dedicated with committed capacity. For hosted we have different tiers. For latency p95 it's workload-dependent; we'll provide benchmark profiles and a proposal for three load classes.
[03:29] Jamal: We'll want traceability: per-request logs, request IDs, and KV cache visibility for debugging.
[03:36] Maya: We emit trace hooks and token-level cost breakdowns; access to request logs is available in Dedicated and Private, and we can set retention windows. We'll include an example console screenshot.
[03:48] Sofia: Encryption: KMS integration is non-negotiable for keys. Can you integrate with our AWS KMS or an HSM?
[03:56] Maya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments, and have integrations for cloud KMS in dedicated setups. There are HSM options as well. We'll send a short integration note.
[04:07] Ethan: Pilot success criteria — what does BlueOak need to evaluate?
[04:12] Liam: For procurement the pilot must show cost per inference, latency at expected QPS, and data handling guarantees. Legal wants proof of SOC2 and DPA alignment. Security wants end-to-end encryption and audit trail.
[04:25] Jordan: Great, we'll propose a pilot SLO doc: sample traffic, target latencies, cost model, and a go/no-go checklist.
[04:34] Nadia: On the DPA, we may ask for specific subprocessor lists and a right to audit clause. How do you usually handle subprocessors?
[04:43] Jordan: We maintain a subprocessors list; we can provide it and allow for notification windows for changes. Right-to-audit is often scoped; we can propose a mutually acceptable approach — typically SOC2 + security questionnaire plus periodic reviews.
[04:55] Sofia: Do you have penetration test reports?
[05:00] Maya: We have red-team summaries and pen-test outcomes; we'll include redacted reports where appropriate.
[05:06] Liam: Pricing approval — procurement needs a clear path: what's included in the commit, overage rates, and a contact for discounts or credits.
[05:16] Jordan: We'll provide a commercial term sheet with base commit, overage pricing, and a sample invoice. Also, we'll flag onboarding credits for the pilot.
[05:25] Jamal: Integration question: can we run a canary to route traffic to Redwood and fall back to our current provider?
[05:31] Maya: Yes, we support smart routing and automated fallback policies. We can share sample routing policies and a canary playbook.
[05:40] Ethan: Onboarding timeline: once MSA terms are accepted we typically spin up a pilot within 2-5 business days for Dedicated if capacity is available, private longer.
[05:50] Liam: Legal will likely push back on indemnity and data residency. We need an acceptable template quickly.
[05:57] Jordan: We'll send suggested language. To manage cycle time, suggest we do a redline call mid next week with both legal teams.
[06:07] Nadia: That would be helpful. Please also include any DPA exceptions typical for finance.
[06:14] Jordan: Absolutely.
[06:17] [10:22] Jordan: (note: fast-forward) Ok jumping into some specifics we should capture: 1) MSA redline owner, 2) pilot SLOs, 3) SOC2 and KMS artifacts, 4) subprocessors list, 5) pricing term sheet.
[10:36] Liam: Sounds right. For approval path I'll list: procurement (me), security (Sofia), legal (Nadia), CTO sign-off. We need the dates by next Tuesday ideally.
[10:49] Maya: Regarding KMS, do you have a preference for bring-your-own-key or do you want Redwood-managed keys for the pilot?
[10:57] Sofia: For pilot we can accept Redwood-managed with encryption-at-rest but for production we require BYOK via our AWS KMS.
[11:05] Jordan: That makes sense; we'll propose pilot-friendly options and production BYOK steps in the doc.
[11:13] Jamal: On logging, what's the retention and how do we export logs into Splunk?
[11:19] Maya: We can set retention windows per-customer and push logs to S3 or directly to Splunk via a connector; we'll include a sample configuration.
[11:29] Liam: On SLA credits — what's the credit calculation?
[11:34] Jordan: SLA credits are typically pro-rated service credits based on downtime buckets. We'll include a sample SLA table with credit percentages.
[11:42] Nadia: On DPA: are there any subprocessors in regions outside EU/US we should be aware of?
[11:49] Maya: We'll provide the current subprocessors list and region mapping. We do have some infra in APAC; we can show where data may transit and where it's stored for Dedicated.
[11:59] Sofia: Also, do you support SAML with SCIM provisioning?
[12:04] Jordan: Yes, SAML + SCIM supported for SSO and provisioning; we'll include the SSO integration guide and sample assertion mappings.
[12:12] Ethan: Anything else blocking the procurement path from your side?
[12:16] Liam: Two things: clarity on total cost of ownership for Dedicated vs hosted for our expected throughput, and the finalized MSA language.
[12:25] Jordan: We'll provide both a cost model spreadsheet and the MSA redline in one packet.
[12:31] Liam: If we get that by Wednesday it's realistic for procurement review.
[12:36] Jordan: We'll aim for Tuesday/Wednesday deliverable.
[12:40] [24:05] Maya: Quick note on performance: we will attach two benchmark profiles — small conversational flows and large batch embeddings — with expected p95 and p99 numbers per model class. Those numbers are approximations but help you pick Dedicated sizes.
[24:20] Jamal: Good. For the pilot we'll run the small conversational and a 10K embedding job to validate cost.
[24:29] Nadia: About the right-to-audit, if we scope to SOC2 plus quarterly questionnaire is that acceptable to BlueOak?
[24:36] Liam: That could work — Nadia and Sofia will mark the exceptions.
[24:41] Jordan: Great, recapping next steps: Jordan sends MSA redlines + term sheet; Maya sends SOC2 + KMS note + bench profiles; BlueOak confirms decision committee and budget.
[24:52] Sofia: We'll also want a short runbook for incident response and escalation contacts.
[24:58] Jordan: We'll include our incident response playbook extract and contacts.
[25:03] Liam: OK, timeline dependencies documented. Any stall factors we should call out?
[25:08] Jordan: Legal redlines and DPA exceptions usually are the main stall — that's why we'll propose specific language to shorten cycles.
[25:16] Nadia: One ask — please mark the commercial items separate from the legal to speed procurement review.
[25:22] Jordan: Yep, we'll send a commercial-only packet and a legal packet.
[25:27] Jamal: Also want a contact for infra provisioning — who will be our SE during the pilot?
[25:32] Jordan: Maya will be primary SE; Ethan will handle onboarding coordination.
[25:37] Maya: Happy to be the SE.
[25:40] [40:12] Liam: If we hit an impasse on indemnity, is there an escalation path?
[40:16] Jordan: We can route to enterprise contracts desk; we often use a mutual cap with carve-outs for willful misconduct. But we'll propose conservative language to start.
[40:27] Nadia: We'll review and come back with three must-haves.
[40:31] Jordan: Great. Last quick item — do you require a data processing addendum that references specific security controls?
[40:38] Sofia: Yes, include encryption, subprocessors, retention, and breach notification SLA.
[40:44] Jordan: We'll include those in the DPA appendix.
[40:48] Ethan: Any preferred date for the redline review call?
[40:52] Nadia: Mid next week — 2026-10-21 or 2026-10-22 morning works.
[40:58] Jordan: I'll send a Doodle with 2 options.
[41:02] Liam: Thanks everyone. This was productive.
[41:06] Jordan: Thanks — we will follow up with the packet.
[41:10] [51:50] (call ends)
notes: Transcription contains minor ASR errors; speaker labels may be approximate. Shared artifacts referenced: term-sheet.xlsx (to be sent), SOC2-Redwood.pdf (link to be shared), pilot-slo-template.xlsx.
